dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Multiple System Atrophy, parkinsonian type (MSA-P) — a sporadic α-synucleinopathy with putaminal neurodegeneration and brainstem involvement accounting for the bilateral INO, convergence failure, and vertical gaze limitation.

1. Multiple System Atrophy, cerebellar type (MSA-C) — if the gait unsteadiness reflects a developing cerebellar syndrome, with the putaminal changes being early or incidental.
2. Progressive Supranuclear Palsy (PSP) — can produce a supranuclear gaze disorder and gait instability, though the absent hummingbird sign and presence of a putaminal rim favour MSA; the rim sign can occasionally occur in PSP.
3. Niemann-Pick disease type C — adult-onset vertical supranuclear gaze palsy with ataxia is classic, but the putaminal rim sign with iron-related SWI hypointensity is not characteristic, and CSF/serum markers were not suggestive.
